title: Stacks: Last In, First Out
lead: A stack is a pile where you can only add or remove from the top. The last item added is always the first one out — like a stack of plates.

sections.heading: Push and Pop
sections.body: Two operations matter: push (add to top) and pop (remove from top). Both are O(1) — instant. Peek lets you see the top without removing it. Never touch the bottom directly.

sections.heading: Real uses
sections.body: Browser back button, undo in editors, balanced parentheses checking, and recursive function calls all use a stack under the hood. Whenever you need to 'remember where you came from', a stack is the right tool.

tryThis: Open a code editor. Push the letters A, B, C one at a time. Pop them — what order do they come out? Now use this to check if '([{}])' has balanced brackets.
